heading: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
content:
ICT (Information and Communication Technology) is the overall technology infrastructure used to collect, process, store, transmit, manage, and exchange information through computer, network, communication, and digital systems.

In an industrial, oil & gas, power plant, or large commercial project, the ICT system provides the communication and IT infrastructure that connects different departments, buildings, control rooms, field locations, security systems, and operational systems.

Main Components of an ICT System

heading: Structured Cabling System
content:
1. Structured Cabling System

    • Copper UTP/FTP cabling

    • Fiber optic cabling

    • Patch panels and outlets

    • Fiber distribution frames (FDF/ODF)

    • Racks and cabinets

heading: Core Switches
content:
1. Core switches - Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of high-performance Layer 3 core network switches serving as the central backbone of the security and ICT infrastructure. The core switches shall provide high-speed fiber and Ethernet connectivity between the MDF, IDF, distribution switches, servers, and critical security systems. The solution shall support VLANs, Layer 3 routing, link aggregation, network redundancy, QoS, multicast traffic management, and centralized network monitoring. The core network shall be designed with appropriate redundancy and scalability to ensure high availability, reliable operation, and future expansion of the facility's security and communication systems.

The Core Switch serves as the central backbone of the facility's IP network, providing high-speed, reliable, and redundant connectivity between major network segments, servers, security systems, and distribution/access switches. It is designed to handle high volumes of network traffic while maintaining low latency and continuous network availability.

For an industrial security infrastructure, the core switch can provide centralized connectivity for systems such as CCTV/VSS, Access Control System (ACS), Perimeter Intrusion Detection System (PIDS), ALPR, Intercom, PAGA, VoIP, Wi-Fi, servers, and network management systems.

heading: Distribution Switches
content:
1. Distribution switches :

Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of managed Layer 3 distribution switches to provide aggregated and resilient connectivity between the access/industrial switches and the core network. The distribution switches shall support high-speed fiber-optic uplinks, VLAN segmentation, Layer 3 routing, link aggregation, spanning-tree protocols, QoS, multicast traffic management, and centralized network monitoring. The distribution layer shall be designed with appropriate redundancy and sufficient capacity to support high-bandwidth security applications, including CCTV, Access Control, PIDS, ALPR, Intercom, PAGA, and other IP-based systems, while allowing for future network expansion.

heading: Access Switches
content:
1. Access switches:

Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of managed access switches providing reliable Ethernet connectivity to field-level security and ICT devices. The access switches shall support Gigabit Ethernet access ports, PoE/PoE+ for compatible powered devices, high-speed fiber-optic uplinks, VLAN segmentation, QoS, multicast management, network redundancy, and centralized monitoring. The switches shall provide secure and reliable connectivity for CCTV cameras, Access Control Systems, ALPR, PIDS, IP intercoms, PAGA, Wi-Fi access points, and other IP-based devices. Industrial-rated switches shall be provided where required for harsh or outdoor operating environments.

heading: Industrial Ethernet Switches
content:
1. Industrial Ethernet switches

Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of ruggedized managed industrial Ethernet switches designed for reliable operation in harsh industrial and outdoor environments. The switches shall provide Gigabit Ethernet connectivity with suitable PoE/PoE+ ports for field security devices and fiber-optic uplinks to the distribution network. The solution shall support VLANs, QoS, IGMP Snooping, RSTP/MSTP, link aggregation, network redundancy, secure management, and centralized monitoring through the NMS. The industrial switches shall be suitable for installation within outdoor and field cabinets and shall support extended temperature operation, vibration resistance, electromagnetic immunity, and redundant power inputs where required. The switches shall provide reliable connectivity for CCTV, ALPR, PIDS, ACS, intercom, PAGA, and other IP-based security systems.

heading: Routers
content:
1. Routers :

Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of enterprise-grade network routers to provide secure Layer 3 connectivity between the facility security network and the corporate WAN/MPLS infrastructure. The routers shall support IPv4/IPv6 routing, VLAN and inter-VLAN routing, static and dynamic routing protocols, QoS, ACLs, VPN connectivity, traffic management, and centralized network monitoring. The solution shall provide reliable and secure communication between local security systems and remote facilities, control centers, and corporate network resources. Redundant WAN connectivity and high-availability configurations shall be provided where required to ensure continuous operation of critical security and communication services.

  1. Wireless LAN/Wi-Fi- Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a secure enterprise-grade Wireless LAN system comprising wireless access points, Wireless LAN Controller, PoE network switches, and associated management components. The WLAN shall provide reliable wireless connectivity for authorized users and approved operational devices throughout the designated facility areas. The system shall support Wi-Fi 6 or higher, WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise security, 802.1X authentication, VLAN segmentation, multiple SSIDs, QoS, seamless roaming, centralized configuration, RF management, and network monitoring. The wireless infrastructure shall be designed to provide adequate coverage, capacity, security, and availability while maintaining appropriate segregation from critical security and operational networks.

  2. Network controllers - Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a centralized network management and control platform for monitoring and managing the complete network infrastructure. The system shall provide centralized visibility and administration of core, distribution, access, industrial switches, routers, wireless LAN controllers, and associated network devices. The platform shall support real-time device and link monitoring, network topology visualization, performance analysis, fault and alarm management, configuration backup, firmware management, event logging, reporting, and secure role-based administration. The Network Controller shall provide centralized network visibility and assist in maintaining the availability, reliability, and operational performance of the facility's security and ICT network infrastructure

heading: Data Center / Server Infrastructure
content:
1. Data Center / Server Infrastructure

    1. Servers : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of enterprise-grade rack-mounted servers to provide centralized computing, application hosting, database, and management services for the facility's ICT and security systems. The servers shall be equipped with high-performance processors, ECC memory, enterprise-grade storage configured with suitable RAID protection, redundant power supplies, multiple network interfaces, and dedicated remote management capabilities. The server infrastructure shall support the required security applications, including VMS, ACS, PSIM, NMS, Intercom, PAGA, database, and other associated services. The solution shall provide high availability, secure operation, scalability, centralized backup, and reliable performance to support continuous operation of critical security and communication systems.

    2. Storage systems: Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of an enterprise-grade centralized storage system designed to provide secure, reliable, and scalable storage for CCTV video recordings and other critical security and ICT application data. The storage solution shall support enterprise-grade HDD/SSD drives, appropriate RAID protection, redundant controllers and power supplies, high-speed network connectivity, centralized monitoring, and online capacity expansion. The system shall be sized based on the required number of cameras, recording resolution, frame rate, compression, recording mode, and specified retention period. The storage architecture shall provide adequate performance, data protection, high availability, and scalability to support the continuous operation of critical security systems.

    3. Network Attached Storage (NAS) : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of an enterprise-grade Network Attached Storage system to provide centralized, secure, and scalable file-level storage for the facility's ICT and security infrastructure. The NAS shall support enterprise-grade HDD/SSD drives with suitable RAID protection, redundant network interfaces, expandable storage capacity, automated backup, snapshot, data replication, and centralized monitoring capabilities. The system shall support standard network storage protocols such as SMB/CIFS and NFS and shall provide secure role-based access to authorized users and applications. The NAS shall be suitable for backup and archival requirements associated with VMS, ACS, PSIM, NMS, Intercom, and other critical security and ICT systems.

    4. Server racks : Supply, installation, configuration, and commissioning of heavy-duty 19-inch server racks suitable for housing servers, storage systems, network switches, routers, patch panels, PDUs, UPS systems, and associated ICT/security equipment. The racks shall be constructed from robust steel materials and shall include lockable front and rear doors, removable side panels, adjustable mounting rails, vertical and horizontal cable management, grounding provisions, ventilation, and adequate load-bearing capacity. Rack dimensions and U-height shall be selected based on the installed equipment and future expansion requirements. The complete rack assembly shall provide secure equipment housing, efficient cable organization, proper airflow, ease of maintenance, and a professional installation suitable for critical industrial security and ICT environments.

    5. KVM systems: Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a rack-mounted Keyboard, Video, and Mouse (KVM) system to provide centralized local management and control of multiple servers and computing equipment through a single operator console. The KVM system shall support the required number of server connections, high-resolution video, USB keyboard and mouse control, on-screen server selection, secure access, and rack-mounted installation. The system shall be suitable for administration and troubleshooting of VMS, ACS, PSIM, NMS, Intercom, database, and other critical security and ICT servers, thereby reducing equipment footprint and improving operational efficiency within the server/network room.

    6. UPS and power distribution : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of an online double-conversion UPS and associated power distribution system to provide reliable, continuous, and conditioned power to critical ICT, network, security, and communication equipment. The system shall include appropriately sized UPS units, battery banks, UPS distribution panels, rack-mounted PDUs, circuit protection, surge protection, monitoring, and associated cabling. The UPS system shall provide protection against power interruptions, voltage fluctuations, surges, overloads, and other electrical disturbances. The system shall be sized based on the calculated critical load, required autonomy, and future expansion allowance. Where required, redundant UPS and dual-PDU arrangements shall be provided for equipment with dual power supplies to ensure high availability and continuity of critical security and ICT services.

heading: Network Security
content:
1. Network Security

    1. Firewalls : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of enterprise-grade Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW) to provide secure and controlled communication between the facility's internal security/ICT networks, corporate WAN/MPLS, Internet, remote facilities, and other external networks. The firewall solution shall provide stateful traffic inspection, network segmentation, access control policies, NAT, VPN, intrusion prevention, application control, secure administration, centralized logging, and security monitoring. The firewall shall support high-availability operation and redundant connectivity where required to ensure continuous protection and reliable operation of critical systems, including CCTV/VMS, ACS, PIDS, ALPR, PSIM, Intercom, PAGA, servers, and network management infrastructure.

    2. Intrusion Prevention/Detection Systems (IPS/IDS) : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of an enterprise-grade Intrusion Detection and Prevention System to continuously monitor and protect the facility's network infrastructure against unauthorized access, malicious traffic, network attacks, exploits, malware, scanning activities, and other security threats. The solution shall support signature-based and anomaly-based detection, real-time alerting, deep packet inspection, automated threat prevention, centralized logging, reporting, and integration with SIEM/NMS/SOC platforms. The IDS/IPS shall be appropriately positioned within the network security architecture to protect critical ICT and security systems, including CCTV/VMS, ACS, PIDS, ALPR, PSIM, Intercom, PAGA, servers, and network management infrastructure. For critical industrial environments, the solution shall be configured in accordance with approved security policies to ensure effective threat protection without adversely affecting the operation of essential systems.

    3. VPN: Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a secure VPN solution to provide encrypted communication between remote industrial facilities, corporate networks, data centers, control centers, and authorized remote users. The VPN solution shall support secure site-to-site IPsec connectivity and remote-access VPN capabilities, with strong encryption, secure authentication, access control, centralized logging, monitoring, and high-availability features where required. The solution shall enable secure and controlled communication for critical ICT and security applications, including CCTV/VMS, ACS, PIDS, ALPR, PSIM, Intercom, PAGA, NMS, and associated network services, while ensuring that remote access is restricted to authorized users and approved network resources.

    4. Network access control: Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a centralized Network Access Control solution to provide secure and policy-based access to the facility's wired and wireless network infrastructure. The NAC system shall authenticate and authorize users and devices using 802.1X, RADIUS, certificate-based authentication, MAC authentication, or other approved methods. The solution shall support device profiling, role-based access control, dynamic VLAN assignment, guest access, endpoint compliance assessment, quarantine of unauthorized or non-compliant devices, centralized monitoring, logging, and reporting. The NAC solution shall integrate with network switches, wireless infrastructure, Active Directory/RADIUS, NMS, and SIEM platforms where required. The system shall be configured to protect critical security networks while accommodating devices that do not support standard 802.1X authentication.

    5. Antivirus/endpoint security: Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of an enterprise-grade endpoint protection solution to safeguard servers, workstations, laptops, and other authorized endpoint devices against viruses, malware, ransomware, spyware, unauthorized applications, and other cybersecurity threats. The solution shall provide real-time protection, behavioral and heuristic threat detection, anti-ransomware protection, host firewall capabilities, application and device control, centralized policy management, automated security updates, endpoint monitoring, threat quarantine, incident response, and comprehensive reporting. The endpoint security platform shall support centralized management and integration with the organization's SIEM/SOC infrastructure where required. Security policies shall be configured in coordination with application vendors to ensure that protection mechanisms do not adversely affect the operation of critical security applications such as VMS, ACS, PSIM, NMS, Intercom, and PAGA.

    6. Security monitoring : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a centralized security monitoring platform to provide real-time monitoring, alarm management, event correlation, system health monitoring, and operational control of the facility's integrated security infrastructure. The system shall interface with CCTV/VSS, Access Control, PIDS, ALPR, Intercom, PAGA, and other approved security systems to provide centralized visibility of alarms, events, equipment status, and associated video information. The solution shall support configurable alarm priorities, graphical alarm visualization, operator acknowledgment and response workflows, event recording, audit trails, reporting, role-based access control, and centralized system health monitoring. The platform shall be scalable and capable of integration with PSIM, VMS, NMS, SIEM, and other security management platforms as required.

heading: Communication Systems
content:
1. Communication Systems

    1. IP telephony : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of an enterprise-grade IP Telephony system providing secure and reliable voice communication over the facility's IP network. The system shall comprise IP-PBX/Call Manager, IP phones, SIP gateways/trunks, associated servers, PoE network infrastructure, and required licensing. The solution shall support centralized extension management, internal and external calling, call transfer, forwarding, conferencing, voicemail, hunt groups, emergency/priority calling, and centralized monitoring. The voice network shall utilize dedicated Voice VLANs and QoS mechanisms to ensure reliable voice quality across the LAN/WAN/MPLS infrastructure. The system shall be scalable, secure, and capable of supporting communication between the four industrial facilities and the central/corporate telephony infrastructure.

    2. Video conferencing: Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of an enterprise-grade Video Conferencing System to provide secure, reliable, and high-quality audio and video communication between conference rooms, control rooms, offices, and remote industrial facilities. The system shall comprise high-definition cameras, microphone arrays, speakers, video conferencing codecs/endpoints, displays, content-sharing equipment, control interfaces, and associated software/licensing. The solution shall support HD/4K video, high-quality audio, screen and presentation sharing, multi-party conferencing, meeting scheduling, recording where required, secure authentication, and encrypted communications. The system shall operate over the facility's IP LAN/WAN/MPLS infrastructure and shall utilize appropriate QoS, bandwidth management, and network security measures to ensure reliable conferencing performance.

    3. Intercom interfaces : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a complete IP-based intercom communication system to provide reliable two-way voice communication between security control rooms, gatehouses, vehicle gates, pedestrian entrances, security posts, emergency points, and other designated locations. The system shall comprise IP master stations, field intercom stations, emergency/weatherproof stations, centralized intercom management servers, PoE network connectivity, and associated accessories. The solution shall support full-duplex communication, call prioritization, centralized call management, event logging, remote monitoring, and integration with CCTV/VMS, Access Control, PIDS, ALPR, and PSIM systems. Outdoor and industrial intercom stations shall be suitably rated for the environmental conditions of the installation location and shall provide robust, reliable communication for normal and emergency security operations.

    4. VoIP systems : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of an enterprise-grade Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) system to provide secure and reliable IP-based voice communication across the facility and interconnected industrial locations. The system shall comprise IP-PBX/Call Manager, IP telephone sets, SIP gateways/trunks, SBC where required, voicemail and associated management components. The solution shall support extension dialing, inbound/outbound calling, call transfer, forwarding, conferencing, voicemail, auto-attendant, hunt groups, emergency/priority calling, call recording where required, and centralized administration. The VoIP infrastructure shall utilize dedicated Voice VLANs, QoS, secure SIP signaling, and encrypted voice media to ensure reliable and secure communication over the LAN/WAN/MPLS network. The system shall be scalable and capable of supporting communication between the four industrial facilities and the central/corporate telephony infrastructure.

heading: Wireless Communication
content:
1. Wireless Communication

    1. Wi-Fi access points : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of enterprise-grade Wi-Fi Access Points to provide secure and reliable wireless connectivity throughout the designated facility areas. The access points shall support Wi-Fi 6 or higher, dual-band operation, WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise security, 802.1X authentication, multiple SSIDs, VLAN segmentation, QoS, seamless roaming, RF management, and centralized management through the Wireless LAN Controller. The access points shall be powered through PoE/PoE+ network switches and shall support centralized monitoring, configuration, firmware management, and fault diagnostics. Ruggedized and weather-resistant access points shall be provided for outdoor or industrial locations where required. Final AP quantity and placement shall be determined based on an approved RF survey and coverage design to ensure adequate signal strength, capacity, reliability, and seamless wireless coverage.

    2. Wireless controllers : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a centralized Wireless LAN Controller solution for the management and control of enterprise wireless infrastructure. The WLC shall provide centralized provisioning and configuration of Wi-Fi Access Points, SSID management, WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise security, 802.1X/RADIUS authentication, VLAN assignment, RF optimization, channel and transmit-power management, seamless roaming, QoS, client monitoring, rogue access-point detection, centralized logging, and reporting. The WLC shall support integration with the network infrastructure, authentication services, and NMS/SIEM platforms as required. For critical facilities, redundant/high-availability controllers shall be provided to ensure continuous wireless service. The solution shall be scalable to support the current requirements and future expansion of the facility's wireless network.

heading: Network Management
content:
1. Network Management

    1. Network Management System (NMS) : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a centralized Network Management System to provide comprehensive monitoring, management, fault detection, performance analysis, and reporting for the facility's ICT and network infrastructure. The NMS shall monitor core, distribution, access and industrial switches, routers, firewalls, wireless LAN controllers, Wi-Fi access points, servers, UPS systems, and other SNMP/API-enabled devices. The solution shall provide real-time device availability, CPU and memory utilization, interface status, bandwidth utilization, network performance, alarms, event logging, graphical topology, historical trending, dashboards, and automated notifications. The NMS shall support SNMPv3, Syslog, flow monitoring, role-based access control, centralized reporting, and integration with SIEM/SOC and other security management platforms where required. The system shall be scalable and capable of supporting centralized monitoring across the four industrial facilities.

    2. Network monitoring : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a centralized network monitoring solution to provide continuous visibility of the availability, performance, and health of the ICT and security network infrastructure across the designated industrial facilities. The system shall monitor core, distribution, access and industrial switches, routers, firewalls, wireless LAN controllers, access points, servers, UPS systems, communication links, and other IP-enabled devices. The solution shall provide real-time monitoring of device status, bandwidth utilization, CPU and memory usage, interface conditions, packet loss, latency, network errors, hardware health, and service availability. It shall generate automated alarms for network failures and abnormal conditions, provide graphical topology and dashboards, maintain historical performance data, and generate operational reports. The monitoring solution shall support SNMPv3, Syslog, NetFlow/sFlow and API-based monitoring where applicable, with integration to NMS, SIEM/SOC, and centralized security monitoring platforms as required.

    3. Performance monitoring : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a centralized Performance Monitoring solution to continuously monitor the health, availability, utilization, and performance of the ICT, network, server, storage, wireless, and security infrastructure. The system shall monitor CPU, memory, bandwidth, interface utilization, latency, jitter, packet loss, disk capacity, storage performance, application/service status, wireless performance, firewall utilization, and other relevant operational parameters. The solution shall support configurable performance thresholds, baseline monitoring, real-time alerts, historical trending, capacity planning, graphical dashboards, and automated reporting. It shall identify abnormal performance conditions and potential bottlenecks before they adversely affect critical services. The solution shall integrate with the NMS, SIEM/SOC, and other centralized management platforms where required and shall support monitoring across all designated industrial facilities.

    4. Fault and alarm monitoring : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a centralized Fault and Alarm Monitoring System to continuously monitor and manage equipment faults, security alarms, communication failures, system warnings, and abnormal operating conditions across the facility's ICT and security infrastructure. The system shall receive, process, prioritize, display, acknowledge, escalate, and record alarms from CCTV/VSS, ACS, PIDS, ALPR, Intercom, PAGA, network equipment, servers, storage systems, firewalls, wireless infrastructure, UPS systems, and other designated equipment. The solution shall provide configurable alarm priorities, real-time visual and audible notifications, graphical location identification, alarm acknowledgment, escalation, event correlation, alarm history, audit trails, reporting, and automated alarm clearance upon restoration. The system shall integrate with NMS, PSIM, SIEM, VMS, ACS, and other approved management platforms to provide centralized fault and alarm visibility for the designated industrial facilities.

    5. Configuration and asset management : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a centralized Configuration and Asset Management solution to provide comprehensive inventory, configuration, lifecycle, and change management for the ICT, network, security, server, storage, communication, and supporting infrastructure. The system shall maintain detailed asset information including equipment type, manufacturer, model, serial number, IP/MAC address, location, rack position, firmware/software version, warranty, ownership, operational status, and maintenance history. The solution shall support automated asset discovery, configuration backup and restoration, configuration version control, approved baseline comparison, change tracking, compliance monitoring, audit trails, and reporting. The system shall integrate with the NMS, CMDB, ITSM, SIEM, and other approved management platforms where required, providing centralized visibility and controlled management of assets across all designated industrial facilities.

heading: Time Synchronization
content:
1. Time Synchronization

    1. NTP servers : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a centralized Network Time Protocol (NTP) solution to provide accurate and consistent time synchronization across the facility's ICT, network, security, and communication infrastructure. The NTP solution shall provide reliable time synchronization to CCTV/VMS, ACS, PIDS, ALPR, PSIM, Intercom, PAGA, servers, switches, routers, firewalls, wireless controllers, NMS, SIEM, and other IP-enabled systems. The solution shall support primary and secondary time sources, centralized time distribution, synchronization monitoring, deviation alarms, and integration with the network management infrastructure. Where required, the NTP servers shall utilize an approved corporate or GPS/GNSS reference clock and shall be deployed with redundancy to maintain continuous time synchronization in the event of a primary server or reference-source failure.

    2. GPS-based time synchronization: Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a GPS/GNSS-based time synchronization system comprising GPS/GNSS antenna, time receiver, NTP time server, associated network interfaces, and required accessories. The system shall obtain accurate UTC reference time from GPS/GNSS satellites and distribute synchronized time through NTP to the facility's ICT, network, security, and communication systems, including CCTV/VMS, ACS, PIDS, ALPR, PSIM, Intercom, PAGA, servers, switches, routers, firewalls, NMS, SIEM, and other IP-enabled devices. The solution shall provide continuous synchronization monitoring, GPS signal-loss alarms, NTP status monitoring, and holdover capability where applicable. Redundant time servers and reference sources shall be provided for critical applications to ensure reliable time synchronization and accurate event correlation across all designated industrial facilities.

    3. Master clock systems : Supply, installation, configuration, testing, and commissioning of a centralized GPS/GNSS-referenced Master Clock System to provide accurate and synchronized time to the facility's ICT, security, communication, and clock-display systems. The system shall comprise GPS/GNSS antenna and receiver, master time server/clock, redundant secondary time source where required, network time distribution, monitoring facilities, and associated accessories. The system shall support NTP/SNTP and other applicable time-distribution protocols and shall synchronize CCTV/VMS, ACS, PIDS, ALPR, PSIM, NMS, servers, network equipment, and designated slave clocks. The system shall provide continuous monitoring, synchronization-status indication, loss-of-reference alarms, event logging, and automatic recovery following restoration of the reference signal. The Master Clock System shall be designed for reliable 24/7 operation and shall provide a common time reference across all designated industrial facilities.

heading: ICT in an Industrial Plant
content:
ICT in an Industrial Plant

A typical industrial ICT architecture can be represented as:

Users / Workstations
↓
Access Switches
↓
Distribution Switches
↓
Core Network
↓
Firewall / Security Layer
↓
Data Center / Servers
↓
Enterprise Network / WAN

ICT is the digital backbone of the project. It provides the network, servers, connectivity, security and communication infrastructure over which many other systems operate.
